evidence: s3_tools.py:189-211. During pagination the break fires as soon as len(keys) >= max_files (lines 199-202, 206-207), so only the FIRST max_files keys are collected. S3 list_objects_v2 returns keys in lexicographic ASCENDING order and filenames embed the timestamp (bh-asia-26/corelight/{date}/{logtype}_{timestamp}.log.gz), so the first N keys are the OLDEST files of the day. Line 210 keys.sort(reverse=True) then keys[:max_files] only reorders the stale oldest slice — the newest files were never fetched. Reproduced: with 24 hourly conn files (00:00..23:00) and max_files=5, the function captures 00:00-04:00 then returns them sorted desc [04:00,03:00,02:00,01:00,00:00]; the newest (23:00) is never seen. LIVE: s3_tools is imported by agents/threat-hunter/main.py:33 and threat-hunter is a built/deployed service in docker-compose.agents.yml, so this is a real data-loss path — investigate_ip/query_flows/query_alerts report the morning's data and miss current activity. Note _load_zeek_events also applies grep_pattern, so for targeted IP searches the practical impact is 'only oldest files scanned for the IP' rather than empty, but a live afternoon attack in later files is still missed.
fix: Paginate the ENTIRE prefix (drop the early break), collect all keys, then keys.sort(reverse=True) and slice [:max_files]. If file counts per prefix are too large, instead compute a StartAfter cursor from the current hour or iterate pages and keep only the last max_files keys. Minimal: remove the three `if len(keys) >= max_files: break` guards inside the loop so the full listing is gathered before the existing sort+slice.

evidence: athena_client.py:62-75. _RE_DANGEROUS only matches DROP|DELETE|INSERT|UPDATE|ALTER|CREATE|TRUNCATE|MERGE and startswith('SELECT'). Reproduced by importing sanitize_sql and feeding payloads: 'SELECT uid FROM conn WHERE 1=0 UNION SELECT table_name,1 FROM information_schema.tables', "SELECT * FROM conn WHERE id_orig_h='x' OR 1=1", 'SELECT * FROM conn -- comment', 'SELECT a FROM t /* x */ UNION ALL SELECT secret FROM creds' — ALL PASS unmodified. Reachability: execute_custom_sql (athena_client.py:375) is called from agents/athena-hunter/main.py:535 with FULLY LLM-generated SQL. The analyst's natural-language `query` is interpolated raw into the LLM prompt (main.py:325 'Analyst query: {query}'). sanitize_value (sweep-1 fix) is applied only to interpolated IOC VALUES (main.py:301-311) to prevent quote-breakout — it does NOT constrain the SQL STRUCTURE the LLM emits. So sanitize_sql is the ONLY structural guard between the LLM and Athena, and it does not stop UNION/tautology/comment injection. A log-borne or analyst prompt injection that makes the model emit 'SELECT ... UNION SELECT ... FROM information_schema...' passes the filter and runs. This is a REACHABLE injection, not merely weak defense-in-depth. Bounding: Athena creds are read/SELECT scoped to database blackhat_pope_logs/workgroup blackhat-pope-dev, so impact is read-only cross-table/schema disclosure within that one DB — the 'cross-tenant' framing in the finding is overstated (single DB, single credential), but schema enumeration and reading tables the analyst query wasn't scoped to is real.
fix: Replace the blocklist with an allowlist parse in sanitize_sql: reject if more than one statement (strip trailing ; then reject any remaining ';'), reject comment sequences ('--', '/*', '#'), reject the UNION keyword, and require the statement to start with SELECT. Minimal concrete change: add '|UNION' to _RE_DANGEROUS's alternation and add checks `if ';' in sql or '--' in sql or '/*' in sql: raise ValueError(...)` before the startswith check. Stronger: use sqlglot to parse a single SELECT and validate FROM targets against a known table set.

evidence: s3_tools.py:267-310. Every public function (query_alerts, query_flows, query_dns, enrich_ip, get_top_talkers, search_events, query_log_type, correlate_by_uid, investigate_ip, etc.) is `async def` but the actual work runs through synchronous _load_zeek_events, which does s3.get_object(...) network I/O (line 293), resp['Body'].read() (line 294), and gzip.decompress + full TSV parsing (lines 65/221, _parse_zeek_tsv/_parse_zeek_grep) inline with NO asyncio.to_thread / run_in_executor. Contrast athena_client.py which correctly wraps every boto3 call in `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` (lines 138, 154, 170, 213). investigate_ip issues five sequential _load_zeek_events calls (max_files 30/20/15/15/20, main path 776-871), each looping get_object+decompress per key — all blocking the event loop. LIVE: threat-hunter (which imports these) is a deployed FastAPI service; blocking the loop stalls concurrent request handling and any WebSocket/heartbeat coroutines in the same process, consistent with the 'stuck on Processing query' symptom under concurrency. Impact gated on threat-hunter being live — confirmed live in docker-compose.agents.yml.
fix: Wrap the blocking body of _load_zeek_events in asyncio.to_thread. Minimal: extract the per-key fetch+parse into a sync helper `def _fetch_and_parse(key,...)` and in the async callers do `await asyncio.to_thread(_load_zeek_events_sync, ...)`; better, fetch/parse keys concurrently via asyncio.gather over asyncio.to_thread calls. Note _load_zeek_events is currently a plain def called synchronously inside async funcs, so the cleanest minimal fix is to make the public async functions offload the whole _load_zeek_events call via asyncio.to_thread.

evidence: telemetry.py:115-125. _RedactingSpanProcessor.on_end only iterates span._attributes; it never touches span.events or their attributes, nor span.name. s3_span_exporter.py:66-73 serializes EVERY event's attributes (_serialize(dict(ev.attributes or {}))) verbatim into the gzipped NDJSON written to s3://blackhat-pope-dev-logs/bh-asia-26/aing-trace/, and the OTLP BatchSpanProcessor (telemetry.py:227) ships the same ReadableSpan (events included) to the external Manifold endpoint. The stack enables LangSmith OTEL emission (telemetry.py:268-272), and OTel GenAI semantic conventions record prompt/completion content as span EVENTS (e.g. gen_ai.system.message / gen_ai.user.message / gen_ai.content.prompt events) rather than top-level attributes — precisely the path the redactor skips. So raw prompts/completions containing internal 10.x/192.168 IPs, secrets, or analyst PII bypass redaction into both the permanent S3 archive and Manifold. This is a genuine partial regression of the sweep-1 sh-8 fix: attribute-based sensitive fields (e.g. athena-hunter's explicit span.set_attribute('sql.query'/'query.text')) ARE redacted, but event-based LLM content is not. Confidence matches the finding's 'medium' on exact field placement, but the code gap is unambiguous.
fix: In _RedactingSpanProcessor.on_end, after redacting attrs, also iterate span.events and redact each event's string attribute values in place. Because OTel SDK Event.attributes is often an immutable mapping, the robust approach is to redact via the exporter as well (s3_span_exporter._span_to_dict) OR rebuild span._events with redacted attributes. Minimal defensive addition: `for ev in getattr(span,'events',None) or []: ea=getattr(ev,'attributes',None) or getattr(ev,'_attributes',None); if ea: for k in list(ea.keys()): v=ea[k]; if isinstance(v,str) and _is_sensitive_attr(k): try: ea[k]=_redact(v) except Exception: pass`. Also add redaction of span.name if names may carry content. Recommend belt-and-suspenders: redact in _serialize path of s3_span_exporter too, since event attribute maps may not be mutable at on_end time.
